question: On identical industry members, does the financing-intensity median increase reflect balance or market-cap changes?
population: Union of exact consecutive source-month industry rows; separate eras/levels. Same instrument and security must belong to that industry under each endpoint prior-month membership. R260 positive complete endpoints; zero balances excluded explicitly vs original R45.
gate: At least5 complete common companies AND common_count/original_previous_members>=0.8 AND common_count/original_current_members>=0.8; preserve all failed rows. Original member denominator verified against membership source.
decomposition: On fixed complete common set, f_ij=median(B_i/M_j), M=P*S. Balance=.5[(f10-f00)+(f11-f01)]; cap=.5[(f01-f00)+(f11-f10)]; sum exactly f11-f00. This is symmetric algebraic decomposition, not causal attribution or sum of medians of log changes.
comparison: Preserve native endpoint medians and eligibility separately, common endpoint median changes, native/common change discrepancy and membership exits/entries. No predictive label reads or model fit.
limits: Historical-proxy, lagged financing snapshot vs signal-date cap, uncertain share publication. Common gate strengthens endpoint qualification; no implicit coverage relaxation.
source_presence_clarification: Both native industry endpoint rows required for common qualification; union-only rows remain unknown even when membership history exists. Clarified during pre-verification, initial summary preserved.
